definitions.explanation: a traditional wooden container used to store cooked rice and keep it warm

examples.japanese: おひつにご{飯|はん}を{移|うつ}す。
examples.english: To transfer rice to the ohitsu.

examples.japanese: おひつを{使|つか}うとご{飯|はん}がべたつかない。
examples.english: Using an ohitsu prevents the rice from becoming sticky.

examples.japanese: {老舗|しにせ}の{料亭|りょうてい}ではおひつでご{飯|はん}が{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: At traditional high-end restaurants, rice is served in an ohitsu.

notes:
おひつ (also written {御櫃|おひつ}) is a traditional wooden container for storing cooked rice after it leaves the {炊飯器|すいはんき} or pot. The wood absorbs excess moisture, keeping rice at an ideal texture — neither too wet nor too dry.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
Traditionally made from {檜|ひのき} (Japanese cypress) or {杉|すぎ} (cedar). Still used in traditional {料亭|りょうてい} (high-end Japanese restaurants) and {寿司屋|すしや} (sushi shops). Some households use them for everyday rice storage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おひつに{移|うつ}す: to transfer (rice) to the ohitsu
- おひつで{出|だ}す: to serve in an ohitsu

RELATED ITEMS:
- {寿司桶|すしおけ}: sushi rice tub (wider, shallower)
- {飯台|はんだい}: wooden rice tub
